/-!
# Littlewood conjectures

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littlewood_conjecture)
- [Bernard de Mathan and Olivier Teulié, *Problèmes diophantiens simultanés*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-003-0199-y)
-/

open Filter

-- TODO(mercuris): This is a norm on ℝ/ℤ, show this?

namespace LittlewoodConjecture


/--
For any two real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$,
$$
  \liminf_{n\to\infty} n\||n\alpha\||\||n\beta\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem littlewood_conjecture (α β : ℝ) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * distToNearestInt (n * α) * distToNearestInt (n * β)) = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
For real number $\alpha$ and prime $p$,
$$
  \liminf\_{n \to\infty} n |n|\_{p}\||n\alpha\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer, and $|x|\_{p}$ is the $p$-adic norm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem padic_littlewood_conjecture (α : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * padicNorm p n * distToNearestInt (n * α)) = 0 := by
  sorry

end LittlewoodConjecture

reformulations.difference: Lean uses liminf as n → ∞ over ℕ, whereas Wikipedia's p-adic statement uses the infimum over positive integers. These are equivalent here; Einsiedler–Kleinbock also explicitly states the liminf formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write f(n) = n |n|ₚ ‖nα‖. It is nonnegative, and f(p^k) = ‖p^kα‖ ≤ 1/2 with p^k → ∞, so Lean's real-valued liminf is a genuine finite liminf. Moreover, ‖kx‖ ≤ k‖x‖ and |k|ₚ ≤ 1 imply f(kn) ≤ k²f(n). If inf_{n≥1} f(n) = 0, then for any ε > 0 and cutoff N, take k = N+1 and choose n ≥ 1 with f(n) < ε/k². Thus kn ≥ N and f(kn) < ε. Conversely, arbitrarily large indices with f(n) < ε for every ε > 0 force the nonnegative infimum to be zero. Including n = 0 does not change the liminf. The exact equivalence was proved as Review.padic_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state their respective conjectures, and both research-open tags agree with the cited Wikipedia article. The distance definition was checked against Mathlib's rounding semantics, including a Lean proof of equality with the docstrings' floor/ceiling minimum. The p-adic norm's rational-to-real coercion and small-input values were verified. Real-valued liminf introduces no default-value defect: both sequences are nonnegative; Dirichlet approximation gives arbitrarily large n with n‖nα‖ ≤ 1, bounding the classical expression by 1/2 along a subsequence, while prime powers provide the p-adic bound. Boundary tests and the p-adic equivalence compiled successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The equivalence depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, not on sorry-backed conjectures. Although the original de Mathan–Teulié full text was inaccessible, its conjecture was independently corroborated by the explicit primary-literature restatement in Einsiedler–Kleinbock.
